signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitical Risk + Jackson Hole Shift
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 160.14, testing the critical 160.00 psychological and policy threshold following hawkish Jackson Hole remarks from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh that pushed September hike odds to 57%. Geopolitical tensions are simultaneously escalating as IRGC navy forces report full control over the Strait of Hormuz, closing the waterway to transiting ships. While JPY COT LF net short of -81,619 (pctl 9) reflects a crowded carry trade, the VIX at 14.4 (low volatility) prevents a broad safe-haven bid from overriding the 275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage. Options markets indicate a strong downside bias with 25d RR at -1.74, signaling the market is paying for protection against a sharp JPY reversal or intervention. Trade bias: Bullish USD/JPY; hawkish Fed divergence and carry advantage dominate until VIX clears 25. Catalyst: China Official PMIs on 31 August. Risk: Direct BoJ/MoF intervention on a sustained break above 160.00 triggers a disorderly unwind of crowded speculative shorts.

signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Commodity Leader
signals.text: The G10 scorecard identifies a critical bilateral divergence with AUD outperforming peers by +1.327% (n=4) while CHF lags at -0.786% (n=6), creating a massive 2.113% weekly spread. AUD/USD holds a bullish technical posture above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.7101/0.7016/0.6971) supported by a restrictive -71bp OIS carry premium against the USD. The AUD/CHF cross specifically benefits from a 435bp carry advantage as the SNB remains at 0.00% versus the RBA's 4.35%. Retail sentiment shows an extreme 95% short position on AUD/CHF, diverging from the institutional trend and suggesting a high risk of a retail short-squeeze. Trade bias: Long AUD/CHF; massive carry premium and strong G10 outperformance support trend extension. Catalyst: RBNZ Meeting 2 September for regional cross-asset spillover. Risk: Sharp rise in VIX above 25 triggers a flight to CHF safe-haven assets, rapidly compressing the carry spread.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Positioning Extreme + Options VRP
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3532, holding just below its SMA20 at 1.3540 after failing to maintain its recent upside momentum. COT LF net long positioning has reached +56,839, placing it in the 96th percentile (z +1.58) of its 52-week range—a crowded institutional long that leaves the pair vulnerable to profit-taking. Despite this positioning, the options market shows a significant Volatility Risk Premium (VRP) of +6.0%, with IV at 11.0% vs HV30 of 5.0%, indicating heavy demand for downside protection. The pair's carry profile is neutral at +0bp (SONIA vs SOFR), removing a key structural support for further gains if the Fed's Warsh-led hawkishness persists. Trade bias: Neutral/Bearish GBP/USD; crowded long positioning and elevated hedging costs suggest a near-term ceiling. Catalyst: US August Jobs data on Friday. Risk: A clean break and daily close above the SMA20 (1.3540) invalidates the exhaustion thesis.

signals.title: EUR/USD — COT vs ESI Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD has declined to 1.1585, moving below its SMA20 (1.1593) following the shift in Fed policy expectations at Jackson Hole. COT data shows a massive WoW reduction in positioning, with LF net falling -55,635 to -55,311, pushing the currency into the 3rd percentile (z -2.28) of its 52-week range. This extreme speculative shorting contradicts a moderately positive Economic Surprise Index (ESI) of +12.7, where Eurozone data continues to outperform expectations relative to the USD ESI of -10.0. The 135bp carry advantage in favor of the USD remains the primary driver of the pair's downward pressure despite the resilient macro data. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; extreme spec selling and USD carry advantage outweigh local data beats. Catalyst: ECB Meeting 10 September. Risk: Short covering triggered by an upside miss in US macro data, targeting the SMA200 at 1.1637.
